synthesis.overall_assessment: The assigned memo has strong architectural direction, explicit stale-canon retirements, identity separation, source-canonical rendering, and several useful negative constraints. It is not implementation-assured: its PlanUnit acceptance criteria validate migration structure rather than behavior, major event/session/security/concurrency/privacy/failure contracts remain open, and its own owner authority is contradictory.
systemic_gaps: Behavior-level acceptance oracles are absent from RTIM-002 through RTIM-039; migration/index validation cannot prove product semantics.
State-machine, atomicity, idempotency, partial-failure, and recovery rules are missing across event replay, preview sessions, mutation focus, patching, scheduling, and blocked outcomes.
Security/privacy contracts are incomplete at thin-client APIs, loopback preview serving, preview bridges, browser evidence, account identity, memory, deep links, and generated SVG/Mermaid boundaries.
Cross-document owner and consumer closure is expressed as hints and ContractRefs, while unblocks are empty and the memo contradicts itself about whether it owns behavior or only routes it.
The final segment's required-source-unit list omits RTIM-001 and generated-tail content that occupy most of its assigned core range.
explicit_non_gaps: Provider, storage, tool-governance, graph, and source-canonical rendering direction is materially explicit.
Thin clients are forbidden from direct provider/tool/patch access.
Generated previews have an internal-origin, CSP, sanitization, cookie-separation, metadata, and bridge-allowlist baseline.
Obsolete provider, terminal/editor, bottom-panel-browser, WYSIWYG, hidden-diagram, and bridge concepts are explicitly retired or prohibited.
RTIM-001 is explicitly retired and prohibited from creating or overriding implementation work.
synthesis.reason: The source itself says owner docs remain authoritative for unresolved product details, while the PlanUnits' declared validators cannot falsify the critical runtime, GUI, security, privacy, concurrency, or recovery behavior extracted here.
